title: Sugrīva Sends Hanumān
story: Sugrīva sees two armed men approaching the mountain refuge and becomes afraid that Vāli may have sent them. He turns to Hanumān, asking him to discover who they are. Hanumān descends to meet the strangers in a form suited to peaceful inquiry. His first action in the campaign is therefore not combat but discernment: observe, approach, speak, and learn before acting.
explore: Scene Discovery: the player examines the mountain-refuge scene and identifies three clues — Sugrīva watching from safety, the two unknown brothers below, and Hanumān preparing to approach rather than attack.
interaction: Prediction Choice: “What is the wisest first move?” Choices: Attack first / Hide and wait / Approach and learn who they are. Reveal the canonical choice after selection; no choice changes canon or stars.

mastery.prompt: Why does Sugrīva send Hanumān toward the two strangers?
items: A. To challenge them to combat
B. To discover who they are and what they intend
C. To ask them for food
D. To guide them to Laṅkā
mastery.answer: B. To discover who they are and what they intend
mastery.feedback: Hanumān begins as Sugrīva’s envoy. The scene establishes observation and intelligent inquiry before action.

mastery.prompt: Put the encounter in the correct order:
mastery.feedback: The order matters: concern leads to a mission, and the mission leads Hanumān into Rāma’s story.

mastery.prompt: Which qualities does Hanumān demonstrate before he even knows the strangers’ identities?
mastery.feedback: The text presents Hanumān first as a capable envoy: observant, articulate, and responsive to Sugrīva’s need.

unlocks: Character visibility: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva. Connection clues: Sugrīva → Hanumān = Service; Hanumān → Rāma/Lakṣmaṇa = Messenger context. Do not auto-complete the relationship network.
takeaway: Before strength becomes action, Hanumān uses discernment.
teaser: Next: Hanumān Meets Rāma — The envoy’s question becomes one of the defining meetings of his life.

title: Hanumān Meets Rāma
story: Hanumān addresses Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with careful, polished speech and asks who they are. Rāma listens closely and remarks to Lakṣmaṇa on the envoy’s command of language, learning, and manner of expression. Before Hanumān has performed any great feat for Rāma, the meeting establishes the qualities that will make service possible: intelligence, self-command, communication, and trust.
explore: Dialogue Discovery: tap/select details in Hanumān’s speech posture and Rāma’s response to reveal three qualities: clarity, restraint, and learning.
interaction: Dialogue Focus: present 3 short paraphrased speech choices and ask which best reflects Hanumān’s approach: threatening, flattering, or respectful inquiry. Reveal the textual pattern after choice.

mastery.prompt: Who is especially impressed by Hanumān’s manner of speaking?
mastery.feedback: Rāma’s reaction makes this encounter more than an introduction: Hanumān’s speech itself reveals his training and character.

mastery.prompt: Match Hanumān’s behavior to what it shows:
mastery.answer: Respectful inquiry → Discernment; Careful speech → Learning/communication; Envoy role → Service
mastery.feedback: The meeting defines Hanumān through how he acts, not through spectacle.

mastery.prompt: Which conclusion is safest from the Vālmīki layer itself?
items: A. Rāma values Hanumān’s speech and learning
B. The text says Hanumān immediately opens his chest
C. Rāma gives Hanumān the ring during this first sentence
mastery.answer: A. Rāma values Hanumān’s speech and learning
mastery.feedback: This keeps the core encounter anchored to Vālmīki while allowing later devotional recognition stories to appear separately.

unlocks: Character Knowledge: Hanumān → Qualities: eloquence, learning, restraint. Connection clue: Hanumān → Rāma = Service/Devotion begins to become available, but player should build/confirm it in Connections.
takeaway: Rāma first encounters Hanumān through the quality of his speech.
teaser: Next: The Search for Sītā Revealed — Hanumān now learns why the brothers have come.

title: The Search for Sītā Revealed
story: After the initial exchange, the reason for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa’s presence becomes clear: they are searching for Sītā. Hanumān now understands that the strangers are not wandering warriors but men carrying a grave purpose. The campaign’s central mission enters Hanumān’s awareness before he has yet taken responsibility for it.
explore: Mission Clue Discovery: reveal three pieces of context — Sītā is missing, Rāma is searching, and Sugrīva may be able to help.
interaction: Missing Story Step: player arranges “meeting → reason for search → possibility of alliance” as the narrative bridge into the next encounter.

mastery.prompt: What central problem does Hanumān learn about from Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa?
items: B. Sītā has been taken and they are searching for her
D. Laṅkā has already been defeated
mastery.answer: B. Sītā has been taken and they are searching for her
mastery.feedback: The search for Sītā becomes the purpose that will eventually define Hanumān’s mission.

mastery.prompt: Why is this information important for Hanumān’s path?
items: A. It gives him the purpose behind Rāma’s presence
B. It immediately ends Sugrīva’s exile
C. It means the ocean has already been crossed
D. It makes the war unnecessary
mastery.answer: A. It gives him the purpose behind Rāma’s presence
mastery.feedback: Hanumān cannot serve a mission he does not understand. This encounter gives the first clear purpose.

mastery.prompt: Which relationships are already shaping this scene even though Sītā is not physically present?
mastery.feedback: The story is already a network of bonds: marriage, brotherhood, and service drive the search forward.

unlocks: Knowledge: Sītā’s absence as the campaign’s central mission. Connection clues: Rāma ↔ Sītā = Marriage; Rāma ↔ Lakṣmaṇa = Family; Hanumān → Sugrīva = Service.
takeaway: Hanumān’s future service begins with understanding another person’s need.
teaser: Next: Hanumān Brings Rāma to Sugrīva — understanding becomes connection.

title: Hanumān Brings Rāma to Sugrīva
story: Once Hanumān understands who Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are and what they seek, he brings them into contact with Sugrīva. The result is not merely a new conversation: Hanumān has connected two parties whose needs can meet. Rāma seeks help finding Sītā; Sugrīva needs help in his conflict with Vāli. Friendship and alliance take shape.
explore: Relationship Discovery: player selects the needs of Rāma and Sugrīva, then sees how Hanumān functions as the trusted intermediary between them.
interaction: Build the Connection: select Rāma + Sugrīva + Alliance/Friendship. Correct choice animates the relationship line into the local encounter network.

mastery.prompt: Whom does Hanumān bring together in this encounter?
mastery.feedback: Hanumān’s service is relational: he creates the meeting through which the alliance becomes possible.

mastery.prompt: Match each side to its immediate need:
mastery.answer: Rāma → help in the search for Sītā; Sugrīva → help regarding Vāli and his lost position
mastery.feedback: The alliance works because each side understands the other’s need.

mastery.prompt: Which relation best describes the bond that begins between Rāma and Sugrīva?
mastery.feedback: This is a major shared-world relationship and should become visible in Connections only after the player correctly builds it.

unlocks: Connection opportunity: Rāma ↔ Sugrīva = Alliance/Friendship. Reinforces Hanumān as Messenger/Service. Future reuse: Follow Rāma and possible Follow Sugrīva.
takeaway: Hanumān’s strength is not only what he can do; it is also whom he can connect.
teaser: Next: The Signs of Sītā — the alliance receives a tangible sign of the mission ahead.

title: The Signs of Sītā
story: Sugrīva recalls seeing a woman being carried away and shows the ornaments that had fallen from her. Rāma confronts physical signs of Sītā’s passage, and the alliance now has more than a general story: it has evidence pointing toward the search. For Hanumān, this is another step from meeting Rāma to entering Rāma’s purpose.
explore: Object Discovery: tap the bundle/ornaments and reveal what they represent — not treasure, but signs connected to Sītā and the abduction route.
interaction: Object Meaning: player chooses what the ornaments function as in the story — decoration only / proof and memory / weapon / payment. Reveal their narrative role.

mastery.feedback: The objects connect Sītā’s absence with a physical trace seen by Sugrīva and his companions.

mastery.prompt: Why are the ornaments important at this stage?
items: A. They provide a tangible link to Sītā’s abduction
B. They prove Rāvaṇa has already died
C. They tell Hanumān the exact location of Laṅkā
D. They replace the need for the search
mastery.answer: A. They provide a tangible link to Sītā’s abduction
mastery.feedback: They deepen certainty and emotional stakes, but they do not yet solve the search.

mastery.prompt: How are these ornaments different in game function from Rāma’s ring later?
items: B. The dropped ornaments are evidence from Sītā’s abduction; the ring becomes a deliberate message-token from Rāma
C. The ring belongs to Sugrīva
mastery.answer: B. The dropped ornaments are evidence from Sītā’s abduction; the ring becomes a deliberate message-token from Rāma
mastery.feedback: This distinction prepares the player for the Sacred Object system without turning every story artifact into a collectible.

unlocks: Story Artifact knowledge: Sītā’s dropped ornaments. Do NOT automatically add to Sacred Objects collection in V1. Connection clue: Sugrīva → Rāma = Alliance/help; reinforces Rāma ↔ Sītā = Marriage.
takeaway: A small object can carry the weight of an absent person and an unfinished mission.
teaser: Chapter I Complete. Next chapter: The Search — Hanumān leaves the meeting behind and enters the mission itself.
